title: Blocked-sender suppression missing for typing/presence events outside WSS draft
description:
Follow-up to dim0, which closed the WSS-draft side of this drift. The same blocked-sender suppression rule is missing in other places where typing/presence events flow:

# In-scope sites

## Main draft SSE typing event delivery
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 1349:

  Not stored; carries no state token. Before delivering this event to a recipient, the server MUST apply the same `receiveTypingIndicators` check described in the `Chat/typing` server behavior ({{chat-typing}}).

The SSE typing event has no normative blocked-sender check. A local user A blocked by local user B can still call `Chat/typing` and have it relayed via SSE to B's clients.

## Main draft Chat/typing server behavior
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 928 (paragraph starting "The server MUST NOT persist..."):

The fan-out step only checks `receiveTypingIndicators`. It does not check whether the typing sender is blocked by each recipient. Pair with the SSE site above — the same fix is needed at the same place since 1349 explicitly defers to 928.

## Main draft SSE presence event delivery
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 1351-1357:

The SSE presence event section has no normative blocked-sender check. A blocked contact whose presence changes still produces an outbound SSE event to the owner's clients.

## Main draft Security Considerations: Blocked Contacts
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 1471-1475:

The Blocked Contacts section currently only mentions message suppression and `receiveTypingIndicators` suppression. After fixing the typing/presence sites above, this section should also state the privacy property: ephemeral signals (typing, presence) from a blocked contact are silently dropped before delivery to any of the owner's clients on any transport.

## Federation Peer/presence Receiver Behavior
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md line ~588 (Peer/presence Receiver Behavior paragraph):

  The receiving server MUST update the `presence`, `lastActiveAt`, `statusText`, and `statusEmoji` fields on the ChatContact record identified by `contactId`. ... The server MUST then fire a local presence push event (as defined in {{JMAP-CHAT}}) to the owner's connected clients.

No blocked check. If a blocked remote contact's home server pushes `Peer/presence`, the receiver still updates the ChatContact record and fires a local presence push event. (`Peer/typing` in the federation draft DOES have the blocked check at line 378-380; this is the asymmetry to close.)

# Already-correct sites (for reference, do not change)

- Federation Peer/typing :378-380 (has blocked check ✓)
- Federation Peer/deliver :257 (has blocked check ✓)
- Main draft Security :1473 (messages-only, but explicit ✓)
- WSS draft ChatTypingEvent (just fixed by dim0 ✓)
- WSS draft ChatPresenceEvent :253, SC :379 (had it from the start ✓)

# Suggested approach

Single commit touching the three drafts. Wording should consistently say: 'if senderId/contactId corresponds to a ChatContact whose blocked field is true on the recipient's ChatContact record, the server MUST silently drop the event and MUST NOT deliver it to any of the owner's clients.'

Optionally update the Security Considerations Blocked Contacts section in the main draft to enumerate the property at the architectural level so future ephemeral-event additions have a clear precedent.
acceptance_criteria:
- Main draft Chat/typing server behavior :928 requires blocked-sender suppression for the typing-event fan-out step
- Main draft SSE typing event :1349 either inherits this via the defer-to-:928 wording (no change needed) or restates the blocked check explicitly
- Main draft SSE presence event :1351-1357 requires blocked-contact suppression
- Main draft Security Considerations Blocked Contacts :1471-1475 enumerates the ephemeral-signal suppression property (or unambiguously cross-references the new normative rules)
- Federation Peer/presence Receiver Behavior requires blocked-contact suppression before firing the local presence push event
- After the fix, an audit grep for 'blocked' across drafts shows the rule present at every place where a typing or presence event is delivered to clients
- The bd-remembered 'blocked-sender suppression' pattern memory remains valid (it is the canonical reference)
